# Rings Network

> Rings is a browser-native, structured peer-to-peer network. Browser tabs and native daemons join one Chord DHT overlay, address each other by DID, and exchange messages over direct WebRTC datachannels; application protocols are namespace-scoped pure state machines run by an interpreter shell. Rust workspace, AGPL-3.0-only (commercial licensing available), https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings.

This file follows https://llmstxt.org/. It is for coding agents that build on Rings or change it: which document is authoritative for what, how the crates are layered, how each target is built and tested, and which conventions a change must keep. Where this file and the code disagree, the code wins; correct this file in the same change.

## What Rings is

- Overlay: a Chord DHT (successor list, finger table, stabilization) keyed by DID. `network_id` isolates independent overlays.
- Transport: WebRTC datachannels, native and browser (web_sys), with STUN/ICE/SDP for NAT traversal. No server sits in the data path; seed nodes only help a peer find its first connection.
- Identity: a DID derived from a public key. Signature schemes: secp256k1 (EIP-191, bip137), secp256r1 (P-256), ed25519, BLS. DID authentication proves control of a key and nothing more: it is not Sybil or eclipse resistance (see SECURITY.md before making any security claim).
- Protocol runtime: `Protocol::step` is pure (state, event -> state, effects); an `Interpret` shell performs the effects through a namespace-scoped capability. Built-in protocols: relay (TCP/UDP tunnels over the overlay) and echo. Applications register their own by namespace: `provider.register_protocol(..)` in Rust, `provider.on(namespace, initialState, handler)` in JavaScript.
- Targets: the native daemon (`rings` CLI with a JSON-RPC API over HTTP), the browser/Wasm node (npm `@ringsnetwork/rings-node`; the rings.rs frontend and its Chrome extension), and a C FFI (`crates/node/include/rings.h`).

## Documentation

- [Documentation book](https://rings.rs/docs/): the reference; source in `docs/src`, built with mdBook and published from master.
- [Guide](https://rings.rs/#guide): the abridged version: one card per runtime and the first commands; the book is authoritative.
- [README](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/blob/master/README.md): overview, architecture table, examples, whitepaper citation.
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/blob/master/SECURITY.md): threat model, assumptions, deployment models, non-goals, and the work required before stronger claims.
- [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/blob/master/ROADMAP.md): shipped foundations and the network-layer and privacy-layer tracks.
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md): per-version changes, generated by git-cliff.
- [Whitepaper](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/blob/master/papers/rings.pdf): the protocol paper; LaTeX source beside it.
- [JSON-RPC API](https://rings.rs/docs/jsonrpc.html): every method of the node API with curl examples.
- [config.yaml](https://rings.rs/docs/advanced-topic/config.yaml.html): the complete generated node configuration, section by section.
- [Operate a Node from the CLI](https://rings.rs/docs/cli.html): every `rings` subcommand.
- [Embed via C FFI](https://rings.rs/docs/ffi.html): the C ABI, its lifecycle and ownership rules, and the Python, Swift, and Kotlin wrappers.
- [Browser Node and Extension](https://rings.rs/docs/browser-node.html): the hosted console, running the frontend locally, and packaging the extension.

## Source map

- `crates/core`: Chord DHT, swarm, DID and elliptic-curve identity, message types, DHT storage bounds. Protocol only: application registries and descriptors do not belong here.
- `crates/transport`: the WebRTC transports (`native-webrtc`, `web-sys-webrtc`) and the `dummy` transport that topology tests run on.
- `crates/node`: the node. Native daemon and CLI (`bin/rings.rs`, `src/native`), browser provider (`src/provider/browser`), FFI provider (`src/provider/ffi.rs`, feature `ffi`), extension runtime and built-in protocols (`src/extension`), onion routing (`src/onion`), JSON-RPC handlers (`src/rpc_impl.rs`), seeds, peer quotas, registries.
- `crates/rpc`: RPC types and the JSON-RPC client. Its protos are plain data mirrors of node types, never behaviour.
- `crates/codec`: the serde wire codec. `crates/derive`: proc macros, including `wasm_export`.
- `crates/measure`: pure local peer credit and reliability algorithms. `crates/network-policy`: the public-network admission policy for egress targets. `crates/gateway`: the native TUN gateway that carries selected TCP destinations over onion circuits (vendored netlink under `vendor/`). `crates/webview`: onion-backed WebView gateway primitives.
- `frontend/`: the Yew/Wasm web app and Chrome MV3 extension, its own Cargo workspace; TypeScript glue in `extension-assets/` and `scripts/` is compiled, never checked in as JavaScript.
- `examples/`: `native` and `relay` (workspace members), `dweb` (its own Yew workspace), `ffi` (Python, Swift, Kotlin wrappers and tests), `proof-demo`.
- `docs/`: the mdBook (`book.toml`, `src/`, `theme/`). `papers/`: the whitepaper.

## Build and test

- Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` pins the stable compiler; formatting requires nightly rustfmt (`cargo +nightly fmt`), and stable rustfmt produces a different layout that fails CI. TOML is formatted with taplo; spelling is checked with typos.
- Native: `cargo build`; `cargo test --release --all --all-targets`; install the CLI with `cargo install --path crates/node`, then `rings init` and `rings run`.
- Wasm: `cargo clippy -p rings-node --features browser --no-default-features --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; the npm package is built by `wasm-pack build crates/node --release --scope ringsnetwork -t web --no-default-features --features browser_default` (`npm run wasm_pack`); browser tests use wasm-bindgen-test in a headless Chrome.
- Frontend (from `frontend/`): `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `cargo clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `trunk serve --release true` to run it. Extension: `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run package:frontend-extension` from the root.
- FFI: `cargo build -p rings-node --features ffi`; `RINGS_FFI_REQUIRE_LIBRARY=1 pytest examples/ffi/tests`.
- Docs: `mdbook build docs`; `mdbook serve docs` to preview; a chapter listed in `SUMMARY.md` without a file fails the build.
- Gates a change must pass (`.github/workflows/qaci.yml`): clippy with `-D warnings` on the native, wasm, and ffi feature sets; `cargo +nightly fmt --check`; rustdoc with `-D warnings`; `taplo format --check`; typos; cargo-deny; Miri on core invariants; the native, wasm, frontend, dweb, and gateway test suites; the docs build.

## Conventions

- Layering: `core` is protocol only; application registries and descriptors live in `node`; `rpc` protos are plain DTO mirrors. Check every new type's vocabulary against the crate it lands in.
- Pure core, imperative shell: keep state transitions pure and explicit, represent effects as data, and confine IO to the interpreter that runs them.
- Lints are declared in the workspace `[lints]`: `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic`, `todo`, `unimplemented`, and `indexing_slicing` are denied on production paths. Never add `#[allow(..)]` for a quality lint; fix the cause (a struct for too many arguments, `Box` for a large enum variant).
- Imports: one item per `use` line, no glob imports. Prefer method forms (`deref()`, `as_ref()`, `as_slice()`, `clone()`) to `&` and `*` in expressions.
- Tests are deterministic: wait for a concrete event (a generation counter, a channel message, a state predicate), never for a duration; run topology tests on the `dummy` transport.
- Comments and docs explain why, not what. When a behaviour or boundary changes, sweep every comment and document that states it in the same commit.
- Commit messages, pull requests, and reviews are written in English. The workspace version in `Cargo.toml` is bumped with user-visible changes.
- License: AGPL-3.0-only for every crate, the frontend, and the npm package (`LICENSE`, the `license` fields, `deny.toml`). Derived works and network services built on Rings must publish their source; a commercial license for use outside those terms is available from Rings Network on request. Never add code under a license the AGPL cannot absorb.

## Optional

- [crates.io: rings-node](https://crates.io/crates/rings-node), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rings-node), [npm: @ringsnetwork/rings-node](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ringsnetwork/rings-node).
- [Releases](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/releases): prebuilt `rings` for macOS (x86_64, aarch64) and Linux (x86_64 musl), and the wasm package.
- Public seed node: https://node.rings.rs. Its external handshake (`nodeDid`, `answerOffer`) is public; status and control methods need its Bearer token.
- Official X (Twitter) account: https://x.com/RingsNetworkio.
